text:
mia: Kicking off network bring-up for APAC-OSK (Osaka) cluster. Focus: transit routing, NAT egress sizing, DNS delegation. I pushed the initial infra plan to the repo.

raj: 👍 thanks. quick note — we need to avoid cross-region NAT hops for GPU nodes (cost + latency). plan is one NAT per AZ for worker subnets, and a shared ASG for jump hosts in a dedicated mgmt VPC.

oliver: Agree on AZ-local NATs. Also we should prefer route-table blackhole detection during validation. I'll add a small script to check for missing 0.0.0.0/0 in the public RTs.

mia: Here's the checklist I'm proposing (short):
- Create transit GW attachment from mgmt VPC -> compute VPCs
- Configure peering fallback for AZs where TGW cannot attach (rare)
- Deploy NAT Gateways (one per private subnet) + egress-only for IPv6
- Add route-propagation rules to route tables
- Create DNS delegated zone in r53: apac.redwood.internal -> NS records to our route53 zone in us-east-1
- Setup conditional forwarders for on-prem via VPN TGW route map
- Validate with traceroute/dig and BGP/route table dumps

jamie: On the DNS piece: we should avoid a global writable zone. Instead create a private hosted zone in the customer region and delegate from central admin. Also plan to pre-seed the k8s cluster entries (node-0..node-N) during bootstrap.

raj: Cost note: NAT Gateway hourly + data-out across AZs. Consider NAT instances for low-traffic dev pools. For prod GPU pools we'll keep managed NAT Gateways. I'll model 3 NAT Gateways x 24h x 30d estimate.

oliver: Routing details — TGW route tables per environment: prod, staging, mgmt. Ensure the TGW route table for prod has explicit routes for 10.80.0.0/12 -> attachments for compute VPCs. Also add blackhole alarm in cloudwatch when number of propagated routes < expected.

mia: Added validation commands to the runbook:
```
# check route tables
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcd1234

# check tgw routes
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --transit-gateway-id tgw-0abc

# DNS check
dig @10.0.0.53 node-0.cluster.apac.redwood.internal +short

# basic egress test
curl -sS --resolve example.com:443:52.23.11.5 https://example.com -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n'
```

jamie: Validation should include: traceroute from GPU node -> on-prem endpoint, reverse DNS for NAT EIPs, verify SNAT preserves ephemeral ports. Also check iptables MASQUERADE entries for nat instances.

sre-bot: deploy-bot noticed: TGW attachment tgw-0abc -> vpc-0abcd1234 creation succeeded (2026-02-14T09:12:37Z).

mia: Good. Now handoff checklist (for oncall/networking):
- Access: grant read-only to route53 and ec2 for infra SRE group
- Run the validation scripts above and paste results to this thread
- Monitor: set alarms for NAT data-out > 500GB/month per AZ, TGW propagated routes mismatch, DNS query error rate > 1%
- Rollback plan: remove TGW routes -> fall back to VPC peering (pre-provisioned) + strict ACLs

raj: One more constraint — APAC region has stricter PEering quotas. I already opened a support ticket to increase peer-attachments to 30 for the account. Ticket #SUP-APAC-4721.

oliver: For testing I pushed a container image with `mtr`, `dig`, `curl` and a small healthcheck that exercises 443/80/53. Use it as a DaemonSet on a single AZ first. Image: ghcr.io/redwood/sre-netcheck:20260214.

mia: Action items:
- raj: finalize NAT sizing + cost calc (ETA 3h)
- oliver: add validation scripts + DaemonSet manifest (ETA 4h)
- jamie: DNS delegation + delegated zone config in route53 (ETA 2h)
- mia: run initial TGW attach and create prod route table entries (doing now)

jamie: FYI — for conditional forwarders to on-prem we need to create a Route53 resolver inbound endpoint in the mgmt VPC and an outbound endpoint in apac VPC, then point the resolver rules to the inbound resolver IPs. That avoids punching holes in customer DNS.

mia: Noted. After we finish I will post a concise runbook with the commands and the handoff checklist. Keep this thread for validation outputs only. Thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: leaving the cost calc here once done.

oliver: I'll drop the DaemonSet YAML here when ready.

sre-bot: alarm created: /tgw/propagated-routes-check (threshold: expected_count!=6)

mia: Closing initial planning stage, will update after first validation run.
